review_text_raw:
A story about an idiot surrounded by other idiots who sound like idiots.

At no point was there any reason to sympathize with Anna and her lifetime of bad decisions that got her into this mess. She's like the stereotypical white person in a horror movie whose phone suddenly goes to static and runs out of gas in the middle of the night in front of an obviously haunted house and says "I should investigate this immediately, and by myself!". Her dumbass ex, her dumbass new lover, her dumbass "best friend", all of whom supposedly want to help her yet they somehow form the main obstacles to doing so, especially the "best friend" who is basically a secondary antagonist for all the help she is. Aside from bit players like the completely unconvincing cop. I thought the cop was lying about being a cop and that that was important as first, but nope, just terrible voice acting, we're supposed to believe that's what cops sound like. Though he's not as bad as the villain revealed at the end, who sounds like a 13 year old boy who got his big brother to install voice changing software for him because he thinks it'll make him sound badass on voice chat while playing Halo. It's that bad. Was it supposed to be intimidating? Was it supposed to be a shocking reveal? It wasn't, just the annoying end to a nonsensical story about thoroughly unsympathetic idiots. Nothing about this is redeemable, this was a waste of a Humble Bundle pick. And they had the nerve to release a sequel? Why, because they can churn out terrible games like this once a week? I hope it at least has an "everyone dies" ending, because after meeting all of these characters, I honestly don't want any of them to live, it would be better for society for every one of them to go away.

[h1] A game for people with questionable morals. [/h1]

The game itself is decent, a very good idea is coupled with relatively cheap jump scares, blah blah blah.

But after finishing the game & looking through the guides for the various endings, I'm just like, "Why is the moral compass of the developers so incredibly fucked up??!"

Decide for yourselves (moderate spoilers ahead):

1. Wanna get the best ending? [spoiler]  - You have to lie to Anna's closest friend from start to finish, fool her into thinking you're Anna and even trick her into a relationship without Anna's consent. [/spoiler]

2. Wanna get an okay-ish ending? [spoiler] - You have to trust a very, VERY untrustworthy registered sex offender and send him Anna's selfies and personal emails at his request and without Anna's consent. [/spoiler]

3. Wanna get the worst ending where everyone dies? [spoiler] - You have to be an honest and decent person, protect Anna's privacy as much as possible, don't get involved with shady people and tell the truth to Anna's friends.
 [/spoiler]

Just let this sink for a moment. 
What is the game trying to teach you with this? 
I got the worst ending and the game blames me for [spoiler] not trusting Taylor. [/spoiler] How so?! My common sense says NO.
[spoiler] No, I don't feel guilty at all for not trusting a sex offender on a dating site, who would ONLY give me valuable information about RESCUING A MISSING PERSON, if I send him photos of that person without her consent in exchange. Especially since Taylor keeps making flirty jokes about this very person. He just comes across as perverted, horny and a sensationalist, and not like someone who seriously cares about Anna's well-being. Even Anna's cheating ex-boyfriend was more trustworthy than Taylor. [/spoiler]

Even in real life I would not trust such a person and would also not recommend it to anyone. The game teaches you exactly the opposite of how to behave.

review_text_raw:
This was my first "found phone" type of mystery/horror to play so I was quite intrigued by the concept and mechanics as a whole. It really challenged how well of a snoop you were sometimes. Hilariously, I kept getting all the bad choices that ultimately led me to getting probably the worst ending possible and I wasn't really upset by that. However, there were some aspects that were a bit troubling for me throughout my playthrough. 

The jumpscares were considerably louder than the rest of the game and there are no audio options available. I guess I could understand if that was intentional since the "investigation" periods are very quiet (aside from [spoiler]the random knocks which were genuinely terrifying because I thought they were happening IRL[/spoiler]), but I actually did have fun just snooping through/messing with Anna's phone and texting everyone, so the cheap jumpscares took me out of the game pretty often.

Also, the climax (and the ending as a whole) just didn't totally sit right with me for some reason. Maybe my focus was waning by that point, but with hardly enough exposition to help drive the antagonist's motives, it just felt very out of left field. (Okay, maybe if I hadn't gone into this game ≈99% blind and maybe had also known [spoiler]what a simulacrum was[/spoiler], I would've had a better idea of what I was getting myself into.) With all that being said, I was left feeling underwhelmed and unsatisfied.

At the end of the day, SIMULACRA was [b]just okay[/b]. It's already very cheap in price, but I recommend you buy it during a sale if you're really that interested. I have just a small shred of hope for improvement on the second game.

review_text_raw:
tl;dr if you want a phone snooping game that is better than this (harder puzzles, better writing) + touches on some of the same themes, and don't mind it being non-horror, try out [b]Another Lost Phone: Laura's Story[/b].

I really like the conceit of a fake computer or phone as the setting for a mystery game, which is why a friend recommended I play this. However, I can't say that I would do the same.

The writing is riddled with typos and unnatural grammatical errors. Like, a lot of these characters aren't even convincingly fluent English speakers. (Also the way their only Black character is written is. reductive.) But it does have its moments that feel natural and compelling.

The acting is... bad. They sound like they're reading off a teleprompter one word at a time, rather than speaking a sentence, and the emotional reactions are not convincing. Worst of the bunch is, unfortunately, one of the two guys whose voice you hear the most. [spoiler](By which I mean Greg.)[/spoiler]

The characterization is weird? IDK, you spend most of your time talking to various brands of Men Who Are Creepy To Women, and it keeps asking you to side with at least one of them. [spoiler]By the way, one of them is a registered sex offender. And somehow, that's not even the reason he's creepy![/spoiler] Even your interactions with the women in the cast are usually about various aforementioned creepy men. [spoiler]The closeted lesbian coming out to (she believes) the woman she has a crush on? That conversation fails the Bechdel test, even if you consider the player impersonating Anna to be a "named woman."[/spoiler] So even though it's supposed to be about Anna, it's more accurately about men fighting over a woman-shaped trophy called Anna.
It may seem like I'm kind of harping on this but that's only because so MUCH of their characterization is either behaving inappropriately towards women or being belligerent to people in general. There's not much to go on without that.

As for the narrative, it was... railroady. I didn't feel like I was finding secrets because even if I found out something a little early, one of the guys would just tell me to do it later. The highly telegraphed railroading in the intro was actually my favorite UI moment in the game, but that was a lot more artful than the clumsy dialogue trees that all lead to a single point.
I did think the big bad was interesting, especially the part about [spoiler]how "a strong individual would simulate a better [life]" rather than live fully in a suboptimal one[/spoiler]. Though I felt like that theme of [spoiler]the appearance being more meaningful than the substance[/spoiler], while present in some parts of the game, such as [spoiler]reporting a colleague for harassment being an issue because it could reflect poorly on the company, or the folder of pictures of random women that Taylor just Has, Apparently[/spoiler], was underutilized. Which is odd, because... that's from your villain monologue—you HAVE to establish those themes in the story up to that point.

There's just a lot that could have been considerably better than it was.

review_text_raw:
The game has potential with its premise.
However, it handles it so, so poorly.
Tried all the endings and variation of the game.

The interface is crisp and the chat messages actually pretty good. Going through messages, characters are both flawed and likeable and the writing does text messaging very well, it doesn't feel too cringe nor too forced.

The thing is, going through someone's messages and all that already does what the game wants; think about what you're doing with someone's privacy. However, by the end of it, it will rub its "simulacra" psychological message in your face in the edgiest, most infantile way. I get it, its a black mirror, its such a smart and deep(TM) plot you have.

But the worst part of the game is the acting.
Upon playing, you will see a set of videos and some people (aka one character) will send you video messages. The thing is.
THE. ACTING. IS. MONSTROUSLY. CRINGE.
It is very, very, VERY bad acting. Not in the way that sometimes in a small game, you'll see a dev do a few lines and it feels a bit awkward, but it's serviceable. No. I have no idea who the actors are, but they feel like very, VERY bad amateur actors trying way too hard to be good actors, but also act like they think they are very good actors. One of the character is supposed to be to some extent a cringy kind of person, but it is not the character that is cringe, the way the actor playing the character is really cringe. I have no idea who the actors are, but it genuinely feel like the it's the dev who just hired his girl crush being like "You have a cute face you're gonna be a star in my game". It is just that tryhard cringy.

Now you think "Oh its a phone game so you'll mostly see text messaging". No, by the time you reach the second half, you'll be bombarded with video and they will be all as painful to watch as the next one. Which is a goddamn shame, because during my playthrough, the messaging back and forth with those characters felt good and compelling.

If you're curious about the game, really, just watch a playthrough online.

review_text_raw:
It's a cool concept and I enjoyed most of it, but at the end it all just falls apart horribly.

The antagonist is just a goofy "social media bad" message that isn't explained in even the slightest. All the "good" endings come from being an atrocious human being who constantly lies, violates privacy flagrantly, implicitly trusts a sex offender and an abuser with intimate details, deceives the police, etc. If you were to play this as if you were actually trying to solve a potential kidnapping / murder, you're 100% getting the worst possible ending and have to start over from scratch.

This is "ignore red flags and trust all men", the game. It's downright crazy that a supernatural horror game about a missing woman fails the Bechdel test.

Of course, the game is one of a kind and a great concept. But it gets most of its value from annoying jump scares. If that's your sort of thing, then go for it.

[b] Pros [/b]:
[list]
    [*]I didn't notice many bugs. Possibly cos the game is designed to look buggy.
    [*]The Investigative nature is intriguing [spoiler] but only at first, after that it feels like you're going to be the next vic [/spoiler] 
    [*]Great if you love spending time on social media. 
    [*]It actually feels like you've picked up someone's phone [spoiler] Except the friggin' thing's ALIVE >.< !! [/spoiler]
    [*]Price isn't bad for the value
[/list]

[b] Cons [/b]:
[list]
    [*]A bunch of creepypasta jump scares
    [*]Annoying fiddley-do games [spoiler] "like complete the sentence / photograph sub-games" [/spoiler]
    [*]Unlikely and non-sensical conversations
    [*]Unrealistic player actions just to get the story moving. Actually, everything will feel weird if you're not into snooping around people's phones [spoiler] Like, why would nobody call the police till the very end??? [/spoiler]
    [*]Unrealistic acting by NPCs [spoiler] especially Greg -_-  [/spoiler]
    [*]Terrible if you hate spending time on social media. 
    [*]Predictable, so very predictable. Especially the ending.
    [*]Arbitrary sounds that fail in trying to be immersive
    [*]Probably about 4 hours of gameplay value, [spoiler] unless you want all endings [/spoiler]
[/list]

Update: I've requested a refund. The game was just too uninteresting. It's just not for me.

review_text_raw:
Simulacra is a found phone horror game with cutscenes that is only fun once. I really wish I could give this a medium review as it is not entirely bad...


Aesthetics:
I gotta say the aesthetics are  a bit dated. It pretty much screams early 2010 but the horror aspect is still pretty good! The acting in the cutscenes is okay but not the best.

Story:
Premise of a haunted found phone is pretty cool. The story is alright but the characters are getting super annoying pretty fast and are just not that believable to be honest. The puzzles are okay but the game really, really drags on and on. Yes, there are multiple endings but when you are done with one ending you don't really feel like seeing the others...
Also the good endings are achieved by not being a decent human being?
The horror aspect gets lost due its sideplots and the climax was actually ... not scary but just weird?

Gameplay:
Puzzle solving. You try to retrive data from her phone and really invade her privacy to be honest. At first it is interesting but I felt pretty bad trying to go really personal stuff of hers.

review_text_raw:
Welp.

I wanted to like this one. Looked promising. But I was underwhelmed. The characters are all kind of bland. I did not get attached to anybody in particular. The acting was dismal. The horror elements are jump scares and borrowed tropes. The antagonist is somewhat of a System Shock (2 avoid spoilers).

I can't see any replay value. I enjoyed the voyeur aspects of snooping into a cell phone. But I never felt like the game elevated itself into brilliance. I was compelled to see it through, but only begrudgingly. I didn't hate it. But I certainly did not love it either. I wish I could rate it a soft rating than a thumbs down. But it does not deserve a thumbs up.
